table_title: For each Nobel Prize category, list the laureates from prize-years 2020 through 2024 (inclusive), with their country and the citation phrase used for the award.
db_analog: SELECT category, year, laureate, country, citation FROM nobel_laureates WHERE year BETWEEN 2020 AND 2024 ORDER BY category, year, laureate
temporal_note: Pre-2025 cutoff anchor: 'last 5 laureates per category' is interpreted as the laureates of the five most recent prize-years available before the benchmark's 2025 cutoff (2020, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024). All six Nobel Prize categories have been awarded continuously across these five years, so each category contributes a non-empty partition. Underlying facts are stable: historical laureates and citations do not change once awarded. Wikipedia list pages were retrieved on 2026-04-29; their data for 2020-2024 has been settled for at least one year and is not expected to drift.
_extraction_notes: Verbatim adaptation of seed #23 from datasets/pkdb_bench/docs/example_questions.txt ('For each Nobel Prize category, list the last 5 laureates with their country of affiliation, institution, and the work they were recognized for'). 'Last 5 laureates' was interpreted as 'all laureates from the five most recent prize-years 2020-2024' rather than 'five most recent individual laureates' so that ties (e.g., Physics 2020 had three laureates, Peace 2022 had three) are handled by the source's own award structure rather than by an artificial cap inside a year. Universe: every Nobel Prize laureate listed on the six per-category Wikipedia 'List of Nobel laureates in [X]' pages with a Year cell in 2020-2024. Construction was rowspan-aware HTML extraction of the main wikitable on each page: Year/Laureate/Country (or Nationality)/Citation (or Rationale) cells. The Chemistry list page renders Country as nationality adjectives (American, French, etc.); these were normalized to country names (United States, France, etc.) for cross-page consistency, and the normalization rule is recorded in curation.json::normalization_decisions. Multi-citizenship cells (e.g., 'Germany; United States' for Reinhard Genzel, 'France; Tunisia; United States' for Moungi Bawendi) are preserved as semicolon-delimited text. Footnote markers (e.g., [J], [124]) and biographical parentheticals (e.g., '(b. 1968)', '(founded 1961)') were stripped from Laureate, Country, and Citation cells. Citation cells preserve the verbatim phrasing of the source page including its leading 'for' / 'For' capitalization and any internal punctuation; the leading and trailing quotation marks were stripped because the source rendering wraps citations in quotes as a typesetting convention rather than as part of the phrase. The seed's third attribute 'institution' was deferred from this v1 because only the Economics list page has a structured Institution column; pulling it for the other five categories would require ~50 per-laureate Wikipedia or Nobel Foundation page fetches and would push source_count well above the per-category-list plan without strengthening the benchmark fit. A future supplement pass can add Institution if the benchmark wants it. Result: 62 rows x 5 columns, composite PK on (Category, Year, Laureate), 0 duplicates. Per-category row counts: Physics 14 (3+3+3+3+2 across 2020-2024), Chemistry 13 (2+2+3+3+3), Physiology or Medicine 10 (3+2+1+2+2), Literature 5 (1 each year), Peace 8 (1+2+3+1+1; includes three organization laureates: World Food Programme 2020, Memorial 2022, Centre for Civil Liberties 2022, plus Nihon Hidankyo 2024), Economic Sciences 12 (2+3+3+1+3).
